meta.title: Operation of BET Surface Area Analyzer in Central Instrumentation Laboratory

sections.purpose: To determine the specific surface area and pore size distribution of pharmaceutical powders and porous excipients using the BET (Brunauer-Emmett-Teller) nitrogen adsorption method for preformulation characterization.
sections.scope: Applicable to Central Instrumentation Laboratory for surface area characterization of active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs), excipients, and nanoparticulate systems as part of preformulation and formulation development studies.
procedure: Switch on the BET surface area analyzer and the vacuum pump; allow 30 minutes system warm-up.
Accurately weigh 0.1–2 g of the dry sample into the clean, dried analysis tube (weight depends on expected surface area — high SA materials require less).
Connect the analysis tube to the degassing port.

Degas the sample: heat to the appropriate degas temperature (typically 80–120°C for most pharmaceutical powders; lower for heat-sensitive materials) under vacuum for 1–4 hours to remove adsorbed water and gases.
Allow the tube to cool under vacuum after degassing; weigh the degassed sample to get the accurate dry mass.
Connect the analysis tube to the analysis port.
Set the analysis parameters in the software: BET multipoint (at least 5 P/P₀ points between 0.05 and 0.35 recommended); adsorbate gas — nitrogen at 77 K (liquid nitrogen bath).
Fill the dewar with liquid nitrogen and position under the analysis tube.
Start the analysis — the instrument automatically measures adsorption at multiple relative pressures.
After completion, remove the liquid nitrogen dewar; allow the tube to warm before disconnection.
The software calculates and reports: specific surface area (m²/g), BET C constant, and optionally pore volume and pore size distribution.
Validate the result using a certified reference material (alumina or silica standard) periodically.
Record sample name, degassing conditions, dry mass, BET surface area, and run date in the register.
precautions: Degas the sample thoroughly before analysis — adsorbed moisture or gas interferes with the measurement and gives falsely low surface areas.
Handle liquid nitrogen with cryogenic gloves and face shield — contact causes frostbite; liquid nitrogen rapidly vaporizes in enclosed spaces causing oxygen displacement.
Do not degas heat-sensitive samples at high temperatures — use the minimum effective temperature.
Ensure the analysis tube is leak-free — a leaking tube causes false high surface area values.
Use the correct sample mass — too little sample gives poor signal; too much may require long analysis times.
Never allow liquid nitrogen to enter the analysis tube — it will cause the sample to compact and block the tube.
Calibrate against certified BET reference standards (NIST SRM 1976b or equivalent) at least annually.
